default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-718.title: Absorption bar after a run
E-718.hypothesis: A heavy-volume bar with a tiny body after a directional run means aggressive orders were absorbed by passive size; the run's participants are trapped, so fade it.

E-719.title: Round-number bounce
E-719.hypothesis: Index points at round multiples attract resting orders and option hedging; a bar that dips to the level and closes clear above it (or the mirror) is a defended level.

E-720.title: Day-open recross continuation
E-720.hypothesis: After the day traded well on one side of its open, a close back through the open means the day's early buyers/sellers lost control; follow the cross.

E-721.title: Wick skew flow
E-721.hypothesis: Over a window, long lower tails versus upper tails show dip buying being absorbed; follow the side whose tails dominate.

E-722.title: Keltner channel break follow
E-722.hypothesis: A close beyond EMA plus k ATR is a volatility expansion that stop orders and trend followers extend.

E-723.title: Keltner channel re-entry fade
E-723.hypothesis: A close that stretched beyond the channel and returns inside marks an exhausted push; fade back toward the mean.

E-724.title: Bandwidth squeeze break
E-724.hypothesis: When n-bar price dispersion is low versus its same-minute norm, liquidity providers are crowded and a break of the window range releases pent-up flow.

E-725.title: Typical-price z thrust
E-725.hypothesis: A typical-price z-score crossing a threshold shows a statistically unusual push relative to the recent window; momentum traders continue it.

E-726.title: MFI exit from extreme zone
E-726.hypothesis: Money-flow ratio leaving an extreme zone shows one-sided volume has dried up, so price tends to revert.

E-727.title: Stair-step highs and lows
E-727.hypothesis: Consecutive bars each making higher highs and higher lows (or lower both) is an orderly trend that late participants chase; follow the m-th step.
